summary: Join our Quantitative Analysis in Economic Policy Training Course to master essential analytical tools and improve your decision-making in economic policy.
lede: Quantitative analysis in economic policy turns questions about outcomes, costs, and trade-offs into measurable assessments. For economists, analysts, planners, and managers who need to justify policy choices with evidence, the course covers indicator and data assessment, basic forecasting, and practical impact and cost comparisons. Participants also practice scenario planning and explaining assumptions, uncertainty, and distributional effects to decision-makers.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals across various sectors who need to justify decisions with evidence, manage trade-offs, allocate scarce resources, and defend policies under pressure.
audience: Government economists, planners, and policy analysts
Central bank, finance ministry, and regulatory professionals
NGO program leaders and M&E professionals
Corporate strategy, public affairs, and regulatory teams
modules: Quantitative Thinking for Economic Policy Decision-Makers
Data for Policy Analysis and Indicator Design
Exploring Data to Reveal Policy Signals
Forecasting for Planning, Budgets, and Service Demand
Policy Impact Estimation Without Heavy Econometrics
Risk, Uncertainty, and Scenario Planning for Policy
Distributional Effects and Equity-Aware Policy Analysis
Building a Repeatable Policy Analytics Workflow
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of economic principles and some experience in policy analysis or related roles. Familiarity with spreadsheets and data interpretation tools is recommended.
